commits.subject: crypt: standard PKCS#8 encrypted private keys without OpenSSL
commits.body:
TCryptPrivateKey (and so TCryptCertX509) could only use our proprietary
PrivateKeyEncrypt() format, so an OpenSSL "-aes256" encrypted key
('-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----') required mormot.crypt.openssl.

- new Pkcs8DecryptPrivateKey(): PBES2 + PBKDF2 (HMAC-SHA1/224/256/384/512)
  + AES-128/192/256-CBC, i.e. OpenSSL 1.1/3.x default formats
- new Pkcs8EncryptPrivateKey(): PBES2 + PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 + AES-256-CBC,
  as "openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -v2 aes256", with 100000 rounds by default
- both reuse AsnNext*/Asn*, Pbkdf2() and AesPkcs7() from the core units
- TCryptPrivateKey.Load tries PKCS#8 first, then PrivateKeyDecrypt()
- TCryptPrivateKey.Save with a password now writes standard PKCS#8,
  wrapping PKCS#1 RSA keys into a PrivateKeyInfo
- PrivateKeySavePkcs8 global to keep writing the proprietary format, e.g.
  if keys are to be read by older mORMot 2 versions
- TTestCoreCrypto._X509 tests with OpenSSL 3 generated vectors

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: test: AES-256 and PDF 2.0 regression tests
commits.body:
- EncryptionAes256: revision 6 dictionary, decryption of a string with
  the file key
- Pdf20File: header, XMP metadata, file /ID, AES-256 without the Adobe
  extension, RC4 refused
commits.author: koxo

commits.subject: pdf: AES-256 encryption and PDF 2.0 output
commits.body:
- new elAES_256 level / TPdfEncryptionAes256: ISO 32000-2 security
  handler revision 6 (/AESV3), written as PDF 1.7 + Adobe extension 8
- TPdfEncryption.EncodeLength() for variable-length encryption output
- new TPdfDocument.GeneratePdf20File: PDF 2.0 header, XMP metadata,
  file /ID; RC4 and PDF/A are refused with PDF 2.0
commits.author: koxo
